findings.claim: FileStore::read and FileStore::write join the untrusted wire-supplied key directly onto self.root with PathBuf::join and perform no traversal or absolute-path rejection, so a key such as "../../../../etc/passwd" resolves outside the store root and is read, and an absolute key such as "/etc/cron.d/evil" causes join to discard the root entirely and write attacker-controlled bytes to an arbitrary filesystem location (write additionally calls create_dir_all on the escaped parent, creating directories outside the root).
findings.proposedReproduction: let s = FileStore::new(PathBuf::from("/tmp/store"))?; s.read("../../../../etc/passwd") returns the contents of /etc/passwd; s.write("/tmp/pwned", b"x") writes to /tmp/pwned rather than /tmp/store/tmp/pwned because PathBuf::join replaces the base on an absolute component.

findings.claim: The "put" branch of handle_request unwraps three fallible operations on attacker-controlled wire data: parts.next().unwrap() for the key, parts.next().unwrap() for the ttl field, and .parse().unwrap() for its numeric conversion. Any remote client can send "put", "put:k", or "put:k:abc" to force a panic, so a single malformed request unwinds out of the request handler and terminates the process instead of producing an error response — a trivially reachable remote denial of service.
findings.proposedReproduction: handle_request(&mut Cache::new(64), "put") panics at api.rs:26 (unwrap on None); handle_request(&mut Cache::new(64), "put:k:abc") panics at api.rs:27 (unwrap on ParseIntError). The kvstore-cli main loop at kvstore-cli/src/main.rs:8-11 aborts the whole run rather than reporting Response::Error for the remaining requests.

findings.claim: SharedCounter::read_or_init acquires and releases the mutex three separate times, so the contains_key check and the subsequent get(key).unwrap() are not atomic: a concurrent SharedCounter::remove for the same key between the two lock acquisitions makes get return None and the unwrap panic. Because every lock site uses .lock().unwrap(), that panic poisons the mutex and every later read_or_init/remove call on the counter panics as well, turning one lost race into a permanent denial of service for all callers holding the counter.
findings.proposedReproduction: Share one SharedCounter across two threads; thread A loops read_or_init("k") and thread B loops remove("k"). When B's remove lands between A's contains_key (cache.rs:77) and A's get(key).unwrap() (cache.rs:78), A panics on unwrap of None; the mutex is then poisoned and all subsequent lock().unwrap() calls at cache.rs:77-86 panic.
